newsitem.title: USA: INDIA SHELVES WHEAT IMPORTS, RAIN AIDS OILSEEDS.
newsitem.headline: INDIA SHELVES WHEAT IMPORTS, RAIN AIDS OILSEEDS.

text.p: India has shelved plans to import an additional 1.3 million tonnes of wheat until it can size up the domestic harvest this fall, the U.S. agricultural attache in New Delhi said in a report released Wednesday.

The attache also said that favorable rains had arrived at the end of July, breaking a two- or three-week dry spell, which should allow oilseed crops to reach their forecast size of eight million tonnes of peanuts and four million tonnes of soybeans.
Attache reports are not official Agriculture Department data.
In a grain and feed update report, the attache in New Delhi said India would complete the importation of one million tonnes of wheat purchased from Australia.

"However, plans to import an additional 1.3 million tonnes have been formally shelved until more is known about the fall harvested grain crop, off-take from government stocks and wheat prices," the report said. "Wheat prices have strengthened in recent weeks and are now higher than a year ago at this time."
Key indicator for 1997/98 imports will be open market prices, the report said. High prices could lead to larger off-take of government stocks, which would prompt imports.
Out of authorized imports of four million tonnes, India has contracted for 2.7 million tonnes -- 2.325 million from Australia, 100,000 from Argentina and 250,000 from Canada.
Of this, 1.7 million tonnes have arrived.
"Detection of exotic weed seeds in wheat shipped from Australia made the government wary" of accepting the final one million tonnes, but the shipments will go ahead, the report said.
